societies.name: Surviving Mars — Human colony with automated food and services
societies.society: A modeled inhabited colony using Open Farms and Service Bots

scope.continuity: Original Surviving Mars with Green Planet; historically documented configuration
scope.period: A supplied, housed colony after Open Farm prerequisites and Service Bots upgrades
scope.population: Living human colonists in the configured settlement
exclusions: Biorobots silently treated as uploaded humans
A wholly uninhabited drone-only terraforming run
Medical and security work assumed abolished
scope.branch: Inhabited Green Planet colony with automated food production and upgraded services

societies.description:
Open Farms can supply food without human farm workers, while Service Bots remove staff requirements from many ordinary service buildings. In this inhabited configuration, housing and accessible stocks support human colonists while machines replace substantial subsistence and domestic labor. It is a partial post-work colony rather than a claim of complete automation: medicine, security, research, manufacturing and maintenance can still require people. Adequate housing, environmental conditions and functioning logistics are explicit parts of the setup.

Human administration chooses buildings, upgrades and resource priorities, so control is placed near concentrated human direction rather than an independent AI government. The game’s command interface does not establish that every resident jointly owns the productive assets. Guarantees are moderately strong within the supplied settlement, but broad uncertainty remains because food routing, shortages and administrative decisions can interrupt provision. Colonists are not automatically nonworkers merely because some services need no staff; useful research, care and creative activity still count. The participation axis remains unresolved, and artificial biorobots are not silently added to the human denominator.

guarantees.basis: Automated food/services and separately managed housing support residents, but logistics, stocks and administration remain important conditions.

control.basis: Human colony administration directs production/upgrades; neither robot operation nor the interface establishes autonomous AI or equal ownership.

nonworking.basis: Automation removes selected staff requirements, not all useful colonist activity; no all-person census is given.

evidence.claim: An actual allowed configuration combines zero-human-worker Open Farm production with personnel-free upgraded services.
evidence.locator: Original-game developer Service Bots clarification and Green Planet Open Farm discussion

uncertainties: Explicit original-game configuration; no imported Relaunched changes or mods.
Partial automation with continuing useful human work.
Housing, environmental prerequisites and accessible food logistics are conditions.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

scope.branch: Machine Attendants with emergency shutdowns and unconditional Free Essentials

societies.description:
This modeled New London combines machine-centered production with an explicit distribution choice. Under Free Essentials, the city supplies basic rations and clothing without payment, and the selected follow-up keeps provision independent of a work requirement. Machinery reduces the need for direct production labor, while human maintenance and other useful tasks remain. The arrangement therefore weakens the link between employment and necessities without pretending that the whole city has stopped working. The guarantee estimate is strong but conditional on available supplies and survival through the cold.

The Steward and council organize the rules and resource system. That supports concentrated human institutional control, with uncertainty about the wider ownership of machinery; votes on laws do not establish equal productive ownership. People who leave the formal workforce may still perform care or other useful activity. Neither the law’s workforce modifier nor an automaton’s nominal labor equivalent supplies an all-person nonworking percentage, so that axis stays unresolved. The paid-essentials alternative is recorded separately because it materially changes access to the same mechanized output.

guarantees.basis: Free provision remains independent of work, subject to supply.

control.basis: Human Steward/council rules govern production/access; equal ownership and independent AI authority are not established.

nonworking.basis: Machine substitution and formal workforce changes do not census useful activity by all humans.

evidence.claim: Machine Attendants reduces direct production labor while the selected necessities law changes access independently.
evidence.locator: New Work Model / Machine Attendants and Basic Necessities law/event text

uncertainties: A modeled, explicitly chosen legal/economic configuration.
Continuing human maintenance and other useful work remains visible.
Availability and environmental survival constrain guarantees.
No workforce percentage is treated as a population participation statistic.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

scope.branch: Machine Attendants with emergency shutdowns and Paid Essentials without an unemployment allowance

societies.description:
This modeled New London uses the same machine-centered production approach but charges citizens for basic rations and clothing. When unemployed families cannot afford these necessities, the selected event choice declines an allowance. Automation can reduce demand for direct human production work without giving displaced people a secure claim on its output. The weak-guarantee score therefore reflects an implemented access rule and its explicit hardship consequence, rather than merely the city’s dangerous weather or an assumption that every resident is poor.

The human Steward and council shape economic rules; machines do not thereby become an autonomous government. Human maintenance and other useful work continues, and the record makes no claim that all formal jobs are unnecessary. Workforce reductions, unused labor capacity and automaton equivalents are different from an all-age participation census, so nonworking remains null. This is an explicit player-selected partial-transition configuration, not every Frostpunk 2 city or a fixed canonical ending. Its material difference from the free variant is the decision to leave unemployed residents without guaranteed essentials.

review_notes: Twelve ordered candidate decisions yield three records through one explicit distribution-policy split.
Original Surviving Mars / Green Planet is kept separate from Relaunched and mods. Service automation does not abolish medicine, security or all human work.
Frostpunk 2’s free versus paid essentials materially differ despite the same automation policy. Exact workforce modifiers are not converted into population nonworking.
UCS was discovered while checking Lunar Corporation and is saved for later stable-ID expansion; it is not substituted into the wrong candidate.
Official EVE crew lore replaces player fiction. Anno/Offworld mods, Elite role-play and a Call to Power sequel mismatch were discarded.
